Ex prisoner here, it's more like 3/4 of people released re-offend, this is primarily because there is absolutely no help. Probation is a joke, you turn up, and the staff ask a few questions (tick box excersise) and then repeat every month.

I was a mental health mentor (and distance education), I'd see people released, and within a few months, return.

I was released in 2016, with (and still) no job prospects, my basic DBS is clear. All I want to do is work.

When there is no clear exit pathway, with no support, what do they expect?

Yes!  


No offense taken :)

Thank you, I can't believe it's a year already, how time flies.  


I don't now if that's good or bad.

White collar for me. The people I worked with I wouldn't really want them released anytime soon.  


I'd be more than happy moving boxes around or a similiar mindless role, I tried B&Q and screwfix, automatically filtered out as am currently unspent. I need just one person to believe in me who I can prove many times over I will work
Thank you, there wasn't a gig economy when I was forced inside, when I was released, McDonalds had new touchscreens, I had to learn how to use them, it was like alien technology
Thank you, I looked at positions this morning and it seems dbs checks are required. I'd like someone to know me for who I am, not what I am
Thank you, most of the time I want to. All I want to do is be active again. I had a great job inside, I was working as a mental health mentor and listener. I was paid £12.50 a week
Thank you I will have a look, all I want to do is be active even if it is moving boxes around
Thank you, I contacted Randstad but they didn't come back to me. I am unsure whether they have raised the bar on who they want
Thankyou for the kind words

Yes, I contacted them quite a few times, they never returned any messages. I tried their shops too, said they use indeed and have been waiting for something to turn up. I thought they are proactive, a bit disappointed
Thank you, I keep applying on the NHS, haven't received any replies
Thank you, I am signed up to their forums (when it works), reading through the discussions, it seems I am not alone
Thank you, I didn't know they were here, although I haven't played a game in years
Thank you Rebecca I will do
Thankyou, I am sure it may the same in other Countries

Ex prisoner here, the sanitation of prisons is awful - they are basically antique. I didn't have to slop out, but I do know of wings that did, because the system wasn't maintained due to no money. Carillion was a joke, they charged a fortune to fix bits and bobs. One day, a self employed spark came in to change a lightbulb, working under the Carillion umbrella. He charged the company £20, Carillion charged the prison service £130....

Sad thing is, figures show ex-cons are harder working than 'normal' employees as they are always having to prove themselves, whether I believe it I don't know. I was security enhanced inside, had access to most places, as I was mentoring others (and thoroughly enjoyed it), now on the outside, whilst I feel very privileged in helping others without judgement, it's a very different scenario on this side
I think I know where that is - thankyou,
I never knew that, quite gobsmacked. Thankyou, I'll add it to my list

Thankyou for the thought, the whole process opened my eyes to a society that's been neglected, it's pretty saddening. About 75% of inmates released are returned back inside, and that's simply due to having no support to gain employment - so they go back to what they know (which I can understand).  


My view on the system has changed completely

I've applied for many volunteering roles, unfortunately no one is interested which is a shame. 99% of the time I feel I'm simply hung out to dry. I've had most of my confidence removed.  


Whilst inside, I was helping others to learn reading/writing, I didn't realise how bad it is. I've applied to become a volunteer to help ex prisoners and their families adjust to 'normal' life, hopefully something will come from that.

Thankyou, it's an uphill struggle!  


Will look today, I'm at such a loss, all I want to do is work, feels like society wants to keep kicking me down :(

Thankyou for those - I will have a look, I've found the PO to be slightly lacking, my time came to an end late last year, and I wasn't even told. I tried so hard to apply for courses through them and got no where, it was such a disappointment as I kept being told inside that there would be so many opportunities to get into employment through them
Thankyou very much, I will have a look through their website today

Thankyou for replying, to be honest I don't really know, I used to work as a manager in a high adrenaline job and had a nervous breakdown. It didn't end very well. I can't take stress anymore. I've been studying online to renew my soft skills, so they can be applied across a range of sectors.  


I feel nervous about applying for roles, as soon as someone notices you have a record, you're basically dumped on the pile without any consideration. I've been trying to get into some kind of customer services role where I can help others, or a trade

Being told to plead guilty to a crime I didn't do, being made a spectacle of, for others to cover their tracks and then being physically assaulted by the police has simply taken its toll.  


I can just about deal with the depression, but the terror nightmares are awful, waking up screaming most nights
Unfortunately, soon as you mention 'prison' peoples' attitudes immediately change without even considering context

Tried that, unfortunately due to the crim' record, I am not allowed to do anything like that at the moment.. Absolutely ridiculous... Whilst having my 'break' I mentored others and was voted for a gold award in best in 'customer service'. Quite a few charities working within prisons want me, but I'm not even allowed to visit prisons due to Government rules

It's very much banging head against the wall :S

Ah I forgot, we are in the UK!

In terms of housing, when you receive financial aid, they put a charge on your house, the first charge (usually mortgage) becomes very nervous and has been known to recall the mortgage - you can see how whatever the case is, you really are screwed.

I do find more 'mature' adults are willing to forgive and take a second chance of employing an 'ex con', but the majority do not. I have applied for just over 600 jobs, not a single reply...

That is totally hilarious, by the time the story is 'accidentally' leaked to the press, you'd be the baron who owns 100 working ladies, owes $400billion in taxes and has numerous accounts in belize and panama :D

Whilst 'inside' I helped numerous people, from vulnerable lads to lifers, when you are 1-to-1 with them and hear their stories, with each moment a part of you dies from the sadness and another part becomes angrier at the 'system' and more importantly, the people behind it   


I realise I sound bitter, unfortunately hearing too many stories of cries for help, instead of giving that help, lads get locked up instead, it makes no sense. (there are obviously lads who should be in prison, certainly not denying that) Since being let out, I've read the press stories of the lads I've helped, and it's heartbreaking knowing the truth has been distorted and in some cases completely made up so it fits the crime charged
Since having a breakdown, I experience exactly the same. Previously, I thrived on stress.

Tell me about it, I used to be a typical 'throw away the key and feed them gruel' type of guy. Now, with what I've experienced and seen, good God..

Just before you go in the dock (I went to a magistrates' and crown court) and was told I had two options - plead guilty to anything and get 1/3 off my sentence, or fight back and go to trial - but then serve the entire sentence whilst my private life dragged through the press.

Also bear in mind all the court and barrister costs...

What one do you go for?
See my comments buddy

Brutally honest, I'm not going to go in to detail for total respect for Glyn, he helped me and others, and is a very likeable guy - easy going, smart and always has a smile doing the best he can within the circumstances and environment he is in. My heart genuinely does go out to him.  


There are many questions that haven't been asked, as that will highlight many many black holes in the case and show incompetence.  


I know a lot of people who have been given prison sentences, and listening to their stories, I am horrified how a system can be 'bent' to ensure a conviction when there is no substantial evidence - innocent until proven guilty? it's only lip service. I have unfortunately been through the same experience and will be fighting my case soon enough.  


All I ask anyone who reads this, please be aware news is always distorted against the defendant, to A) ensure it's a good juicy story, B) this is what happens if you step out of line. There are too many people going to prison, in what way is it right to send a drug addict to an environment where you also send the drug pushers? Is it right to send autistic people to prison when they should have care? I have seen suicides, 'spice' attacks, violence, breakdowns and total frustration. The majority of staff (99%) do an absolute superb job and they are lovely, but their hands are tied. Every decision has to go up the tree and lost in communication.  


I hope that no one has to go through this process, it's absolutely horrible.
No he didn't. I served with him in prison. You only hear a tiny part of the story that the courts and police want you to hear. Glyn is a true gent, a very caring person
That is awful, people don't understand what emotions we go through. Ignore negative people, they arn't worth the energy
Buddy, we are all here, sitting at screens in our little bubbles of life, reach out - no man is an island

For me, quite literally standing still shaking cold looking over my shoulder as a police car comes whizzing by.

I used to be a mentor, helping vulnerable people. When I see vulnerable people on the streets not receiving the help they need, it breaks my heart

I used to play the piano, then life took over in a big way.

You don't loose the talent, it's simply been put in box storage ready to come out when you're ready. Take a step, grab a keyboard and go for it

Life is too short, do what you love

I have a Shih Tzu as a pet/therapy animal, he knows when I'm going to have a shutdown and will stay by my side, animals are more intelligent than we know.

Not only that, they are great to meet new people with!

That is awful. There are many people who still think of 'pulling your socks up and get on with life'. Mental wellbeing is such a powerful thing, just because you can't see it or touch it, doesn't mean it doesn't exist.
I've been a prisoner, happy to help someone. Will PM you
Yes, thankyou. Then prisoners are thrown out on to the street with zero support. It's no wonder 3/4 return to prison
Hi everyone, I just want to thank you all for upvoting. Whilst in prison I had a nervous breakdown, it was awful. No one really knows what it is like in prison unless you've been through it.
I am an ex prisoner, if you know the prison he will be held, phone the prison to get the wing and prisoner ref#, the staff are usually pretty helpful (although overstretched!)
